Accessibility Audit Cost
Accessible.org web accessibility audits cost $100 – $250 per page (or screen) and $25 – $100 for light pages/screens. Our audits follow best practices for ADA and EAA compliance. Our audit price is based on comprehensive manual evaluation using the WCAG 2.1 AA standard (or WCAG 2.2 AA). Audits are conducted in desktop environment with the client option to add mobile.
Our website accessibility audits are fully manual, formal evaluations conducted by technical accessibility experts who evaluate your website or other digital assets against WCAG 2.0 AA, WCAG 2.1 AA, or WCAG 2.2 AA standards.
Scope typically does not include all pages or screens, but rather a representative sample.
We use an automated scan as a review to ensure all issues correctly identified by a scan are included in our final audit report.
All Accessible.org auditors are certified DHS Trusted Testers. The DHS Trusted Tester Process is a manual test approach that aligns with the ICT Testing Baseline, and provides repeatable and reliable conformance test results.
Digital Assets Audited
Accessible.org can audit all types of digital assets:
Websites
Web pages
Web apps
Mobile apps
Platforms
Dashboards

Screen Reader Testing

Audit includes desktop environment with client option to add mobile (iPhone).
By choosing our audit services, you will receive an excellent quality, easy to understand audit report that your team can take action on.
We can add other environments (e.g., MacOS and Android) upon request for an additional fee.
Our website accessibility audit cost breakdown shows you exactly how we determine your final audit price quote.
Deliverables:
Technical Audit Report
Format: Excel Spreadsheet
Includes detailed technical findings and specific issues identified during the audit

$100–$250 per page or screen, $25-$100 for light pages/screens

VPAT / ACR
VPAT services start at $350 for the WCAG VPAT version. We will fill in and complete a Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT) and create a detailed Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR) based on our audit. Our ACR creation service is $350 (for the WCAG version) in addition to the price of the audit for your digital asset.
Other VPAT Editions
Section 508: $550
EN 301 549: $650
INT: $950
This documentation is essential for meeting procurement requirements. We can pause issuance so that your team has a chance to fix issues and we can validate. This results in a cleaner ACR (demonstrating a more accessible product or service) you can deliver to clients.
Price:

Accessibility User Testing Cost
User testing services for website accessibility (and other digital assets) cost $550 per session and are a best practice for ADA compliance. The price of user testing is discounted if you choose Accessible.org for audit and remediation services.
User testing is conducted by an accessibility professional with a disability, is an essential part of ensuring your digital assets are accessible to all users. We offer user testing at a discounted rate when combined with our audit and remediation services.
Service Details:
User Testing
: Conducted by a professional who is blind or visually impaired, using screen reader assistive technology to evaluate your website or digital asset.
Deliverable
: You will receive a recording of the user testing session upon completion.
Deliverables:
Recording of the user testing session upon completion.
User Testing Attestation
Note : User testing sessions include up to 10 pages or screens with a time duration cap of 30 minutes.
Price
$550 per session
$450 per session if you choose us for audit services.
Email us
info@accessible.org
Accessibility Remediation Cost
We will remediate your digital asset at the code level. This means we will fix the technically complex accessibility issues on your website, web app, or mobile app.
To be eligible for remediation, we must 1) audit your digital asset and 2) have full code access. The audit is necessary to ensure we know all accessibility issues that exist (we don’t accept outside audits to uphold quality). Full code access is necessary to ensure we’re able to make all fixes.
We validate our remediation.
Service Details:
Remediation
: Conducted by a technical accessibility expert with development experience. All fixed issues are reviewed and validated by auditor.
Deliverable
: You will receive your code remediated digital asset.
Remediation Includes:
Technical code remediation
Validation of remediation
Note: An audit and full code access is required for remediation.
Price
$750 – $4,500 for most clients, $100 – $450 per page or screen, depending on volume and complexity.
Email us
info@accessible.org
Document Remediation Cost
Document accessibility remediation costs start at $4.00 per page. The price of remediating PDFs, Word documents, PowerPoint presentations, and Excel spreadsheets for WCAG 2.1 AA conformance depends on the document status and project scope.
We will remediate your documents to meet the highest accessibility standards including WCAG 2.1 / 2.2 AA and PDF/UA standards. Documents include:
Microsoft PowerPoint documents
PDFs
Microsoft Word documents
Microsoft Excel spreadsheets
Canva documents
We will manually test documents and fix accessibility issues according to WCAG 2.1 AA and WCAG 2.2 AA standards and PDF/UA. Each document will meet Section 508 criteria, pass the Adobe Acrobat accessibility check, and be individually tested with screen reader assistive technology.
Minimum order is $250.
Deliverables
Documents remediated for WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA, PDF/UA conformance and/or Section 508 compliance, passing Adobe Acrobat and assistive technology checks.
PAC Report for PDFs (where applicable)
Price
PDFs start at $4.00/page
Word Documents start at $7.00/page
PowerPoints starts at $7.00/page

Accessibility Certification
Our website accessibility certification documents are provided free of charge ($0.00) as a result of our services. These documents include Accessible.org certification, user testing certification, and a statement of conformance.
Note that to be eligible for a statement of conformance or provider certification, your website or other digital asset must be fully WCAG conformant.
For a statement of partial conformance, your website must be fully WCAG conformant other than content that is outside of your control.

Content accessibility remediation costs are project-based. Because the work involved can vary from one project to the next, we provide general rates for each type of content. All content will be remediated to meet WCAG 2.0 AA, WCAG 2.1 AA, and WCAG 2.2 AA standards.

Social Media Accessibility Cost
Social media accessibility services start at $1,000. Our services follow best practices for ADA compliance including conformance with WCAG 2.1 AA. Social media pricing is based on the scope of your accessibility project.
One option is we will integrate with your social media team to remediate your social media content (text, video, images, and audio) for accessibility on a monthly basis.
This means we will fix all of your content so that it’s ready for publishing. Social media platforms covered include:
LinkedIn
YouTube
Facebook
TikTok
Instagram
We will remediate content for WCAG 2.2 AA conformance, the highest accessibility standard for web content (exceeds WCAG 2.1 AA). This follows best practices for ADA compliance.
Price
Price starts at $1,000

info@accessible.org
Accessibility Project Planning
Our digital accessibility and ADA compliance project planning services cost $1,500 and up. Our pricing is custom to your project size and the cost includes an organized and structured approach tailored to reaching your accessibility objectives.
Accessible.org can help you with planning and organizing your accessibility project, offering a streamlined service that eliminates the need to hire or train employees who may lack specialized knowledge. We begin by closely collaborating with clients to understand their specific requirements and objectives. This enables us to develop detailed project plans that outline each necessary step, from initial audits to final implementation, including clear timelines and milestones.
Based on client input, we also draft applicable documentation including accessibility statement, accessibility policy, procurement policy, and project roles and responsibilities. By leveraging our expertise, clients can avoid the expense and inefficiency of hiring or training internal staff, resulting in a well-executed project where digital assets meets or exceeds accessibility standards.

Frequently Asked Questions
How much does a website accessibility audit cost?
Most website accessibility audits range between $1,250 and $2,750. Pricing is $100 to $250 per primary page or screen and $25 to $100 for light pages or screens. Because our audits are custom and fully manual, your final cost depends on scope, status, and complexity.
How is the audit price determined?
Three factors set the price: scope (the number and type of pages or screens in your representative sample), status (how accessible the asset already is), and complexity (interactive components, dynamic content, and custom widgets). We evaluate a representative sample rather than every page.
What is the difference between a primary page and a light page?
Primary pages are content rich or interactive pages and screens, priced at $100 to $250 each. Light pages have minimal content or repeated patterns and are priced lower, at $25 to $100 each. Light pages can be simple pages like a privacy policy page or simple
How much does an ACR cost?
Most clients choose our WCAG edition VPAT service, which is $350 in addition to the cost of the audit. We complete the Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT) and produce a finished Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR) based on the audit. Other editions are Section 508 at $550, EN 301 549 at $650, and the INT combined edition at $950.
The different amounts represent the time necessary to fill out the different editions.
What WCAG standards do you evaluate against?
We evaluate digital assets against WCAG 2.1 AA or WCAG 2.2 AA, and occasionally WCAG 2.0 AA.
Are your audits manual or automated?
Fully manual. There is no such thing as an automated audit. Our technical accessibility experts  will evaluate your asset using screen reader testing (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, and/or TalkBack), keyboard testing, visual inspection, and code inspection. We use an automated scan only as a review, to confirm that every scan detectable issue is included in the final audit report.
What do I receive at the end of an audit?
A detailed technical audit report delivered as an Excel spreadsheet, with specific findings, the WCAG criteria affected, and the information your team needs to take action on each issue.
Do you fix the issues you find?
We can support remediation in two ways. Technical support, at $195 per hour with a two hour minimum, gives your team expert help and validates fixes (to ensure the fix has resolved the issue). Document remediation, starting at $7.00 per page, covers PDFs, Word documents, PowerPoint presentations, and Excel spreadsheets.
How much does document remediation cost?
Document remediation starts at $7.00 per page. PDFs start at $7.50 per page, while Word documents and PowerPoint presentations start at $7.00 per page. Final pricing depends on document status and project scope.
Do you offer rush or expedited service?
Yes. Expedited accessibility, including same day or overnight turnaround, ranges from $250 to $750 depending on scope and timing.
Is certification an extra cost?
No. Certification is included at no additional cost as a result of our services. To qualify for a statement of conformance or certification, your asset must be fully WCAG conformant. A statement of partial conformance is available when the only remaining issues are outside your control.
Can you audit mobile apps and other digital assets?
Yes. We audit websites, web apps, mobile apps, software, platforms, dashboards, portals, multimedia players, and individual components. Audits can be conducted in desktop and/or mobile environments.
Do you offer user testing with people with disabilities?
Yes. User testing is conducted by an accessibility professional with a disability using assistive technology, and the session is recorded for your team. Sessions are $550, or $450 when combined with audit services, and cover up to 10 pages or screens.
How do I get a quote or get started?
Email info@accessible.org or use our contact page. You can also try our cost calculator for a fast estimate.
Ready to Start?
We’re ready to help you with accessibility as soon as possible. We provide upfront quotes, clear expectations, and fast turnarounds.
Send us a message and we’ll reply very soon.

What Changes the Cost of an Accessibility Audit
We price by the unique page templates and user journeys a person has to test, not by how many URLs your site has. Up to 5 templates fit the
$500 Quick Audit
, and up to 25 templates or key flows fit the $2,000 Complete Audit. Every package tests to WCAG 2.2 AA and reports against the rule you answer to, such as the
ADA Title II web rule
,
Section 508

European Accessibility Act
.

document accessibility testing
and

accessibility remediation

dashboard
Templates and user flows, not URL count
A large blog built on a handful of templates can cost less to audit than a small web app with sign-up, search, checkout and a dashboard.
touch_app
Interactive components
Carts, filters, modals, date pickers, chat widgets and third-party embeds need keyboard and screen reader testing. Most blockers hide here, so the Complete Audit covers them with JAWS, NVDA, VoiceOver and keyboard-only passes.
gavel
The standard you have to meet
ADA Title II points to WCAG 2.1 AA, Section 508 to WCAG 2.0 AA and the EAA to EN 301 549. The same packages cover every standard.
picture_as_pdf
Documents and PDFs
PDFs, Word and PowerPoint files are tested separately from web pages, including NVDA screen reader passes. PDF remediation is quoted after scoping.
description
Procurement paperwork
A VPAT or Accessibility Conformance Report is quoted on top of the audit, because every criterion has to be documented.
build
Fixes and re-tests
Fixing issues is a separate, quoted piece of work, done by your team or ours. The Complete Audit includes a re-test of fixed issues so you leave with evidence.

Frequently Asked Questions
expand_more
How do you decide between the Quick Audit and Complete Audit?
We scope the work first — pages, templates, components — and recommend the
Quick Accessibility Audit
($500, up to 5 templates) when a small marketing site needs a clear top-10 issues list, or the
Complete Accessibility Audit
($2,000, up to 25 templates or key flows) when checkout, dashboards or multi-step journeys need full keyboard and screen reader coverage. Not sure yet? Book a
free 30-minute call
to talk it through; if you already have a scan or another vendor’s report and need a live technical review, book the
$100 one-hour consultation
.
expand_more
What does each package cost?
Your first conversation is a
free 30-minute call
to talk through where you stand, scope a project and get a quote. The
1-Hour Consultation
is $100, a technical working session to walk through an audit, talk with a developer or review issues live. The Quick Audit is $500 for small marketing sites with up to 5 representative pages. The Complete Audit is $2,000 and covers larger or more complex sites, including full
Shopify storefront and checkout
coverage, or a
WordPress Accessibility Audit
for themes and builders. Need a standalone
VPAT/ACR
or PDF remediation? Ask when we scope — those are available as add-ons. Web apps with unusual interaction patterns may need a custom quote. We will tell you the number before you commit.
expand_more
Is there a minimum engagement?
No ongoing contract is required. You can start with a single Quick Audit if that is what you need. Some clients keep us on for re-audits after each release, or move from audit into remediation and monitoring; that is optional, not a lock-in.
expand_more
Do you offer a compliance guarantee?
We do not sell “guaranteed compliance” — nobody honestly can, because accessibility depends on content that changes daily. What we do provide is documented WCAG 2.2 findings, severity ranking, remediation guidance and a re-test of fixed issues so you have evidence for lawyers, buyers and procurement teams.
expand_more
Can the $100 consultation apply toward a paid audit later?
Often, yes — ask when you
book the consultation
and we will factor it in when scoping your Quick or Complete Audit.
expand_more
Is the Complete Audit only for Shopify stores?
No — it is our flagship offer for any website or app, and it is purpose-built with full coverage for Shopify storefronts and checkout flows. See our dedicated
Shopify Accessibility Audit
page ($2,000). WordPress and WooCommerce sites can use the same Complete package or start with a $500 Quick Audit; details are on the
WordPress Accessibility Audit
page.
expand_more
How much does an accessibility audit cost?
It depends mainly on how many unique templates and user flows need manual testing, not on how many URLs your site has. Our fixed prices are $500 for a
Quick Accessibility Audit
(up to 5 page templates) and $2,000 for a
Complete Accessibility Audit
(up to 25 templates or key user flows, with a re-test), plus a $100
1-hour consultation
if you want a technical working session first (an audit walkthrough or a live review with a specialist). Scoping questions and quotes start with a
free 30-minute call
. Larger platforms get a written quote before any work starts. For market rates and hidden extras, read our
accessibility audit cost guide
.
expand_more
Do you charge by the hour?
No. Audits are sold as fixed-price packages, so you know the full cost before we start. Only Enterprise programs (several products, remediation sprints, monitoring or VPAT/ACR work) are custom-quoted after a free
accessibility needs assessment
.
expand_more
Why does a manual audit cost more than a free accessibility scan?
Free scanners only flag issues a machine can detect. The
W3C Web Accessibility Initiative
says evaluation tools assist testing but cannot determine accessibility on their own. A free scan can surface obvious issues before a call; a manual audit still tests keyboard paths, screen readers (JAWS, NVDA, VoiceOver) and whether real users can complete tasks. That is what produces evidence you can stand behind. See also the “Why a free scan is not the same as an audit” section above.
expand_more
Is the price different for ADA, Section 508 or EAA audits?
No. The same packages cover each standard. We test to WCAG 2.2 AA and report against the rule you answer to: WCAG 2.1 AA under the
ADA Title II web rule
(compliance dates April 26, 2027 / April 26, 2028), WCAG 2.0 AA for
Section 508
, or EN 301 549 for the European Accessibility Act. Tell us which rule applies when you book.
expand_more
How do I get a quote for a larger site or web app?
Send your URL, the platforms involved and any deadline through the free
accessibility needs assessment
. Prefer to talk first? Book a
free 30-minute call
. We reply with a written accessibility audit pricing quote, usually within 2 business days.
expand_more
What is the difference between the free 30-minute call and the $100 consultation?
The
free 30-minute call
is the first discussion: where you stand, what to scope, and how to start a project or get a quote. The
$100 one-hour consultation
is a technical working session — walking through an audit or its findings, talking with a developer, or reviewing website issues live. Pick the free call if you are exploring; pick the $100 hour when you need expert technical answers now.
expand_more
Who performs the accessibility audits at HalfAccessible?
Audits are founder-led by Mohammad Shadab Saifi, who holds
IAAP
CPACC, WAS and CPWA credentials and is a DHS Section 508 Trusted Tester, with 10+ years in digital accessibility. You work with specialists who map every issue to WCAG 2.2 and re-test fixes — not an overlay widget.
expand_more
Is a Shopify accessibility audit a different price?
The dedicated
Shopify Accessibility Audit
is $2,000 and covers storefront templates, cart and checkout flows with the same Complete Audit depth. It is not sold as a “free” scan or an hourly retainer.
expand_more
Can I start with an automated score before paying for an audit?
Yes. Run a free automated accessibility check first if you like, then bring the results to a
free 30-minute call
or the
$100 technical consultation
. Automated scores complement a manual audit; they do not replace keyboard and screen reader testing.
expand_more
How does accessibility audit cost compare to an ADA demand letter?
A planned audit is usually far cheaper than reacting after a demand letter or lawsuit. Public trackers show steady filing volume (EcomBack counted 2,045 ADA website lawsuits in U.S. courts from January to June 2026); defense, experts and forced remediation after the fact routinely exceed a $500 or $2,000 audit. If you already have a letter, see
ADA lawsuit remediation
and start with the needs assessment or a free 30-minute call.
expand_more
How do I compare pricing for accessibility audits?
Compare what each quote covers, not just the number. Check how many templates and user flows are tested, whether a person tests with a keyboard and screen readers (not only an automated scan), what the report includes (WCAG 2.2 mapping, fix guidance, a re-test of fixes) and who does the work. accessibility audit cost guide

Conduct an audit to measure compliance with laws, guidelines, and standards
ADA
The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) is a civil rights and equal opportunity law prohibiting discrimination against people with disabilities in the United States.
AODA
The Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA) is a law established in Ontario, Canada to enforce accessibility standards for government, businesses, nonprofits, private and public sector organizations.
EAA
The European Accessibility Act (EAA) is a directive of the European Union that aims to improve accessibility across all 27 EU member states and for the organizations doing business there.
EN 301 549
EN 301 549 is the European standard of Accessibility requirements for Information and Communications Technology (ICT) products and services in the European Union.
Section 508
Section 508 is a sub-section of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 that prohibits discrimination on the basis of disability in federal programs or programs receiving federal aid or employment in the United States.
WCAG
The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines were developed by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) and are widely accepted as the go-to standard for digital accessibility conformance.

Work with Deque to conduct an audit
to identify any issues and receive expert guidance on remediation and next steps. For legal matters, always consult with a qualified attorney for advice specific to your situation.
A prospect requires our digital property to be accessible. What should we do?
Start by confirming your accessibility status with a Deque audit. Our experts can help you address issues, document compliance, and provide an ACR (based on a
VPAT
) to share with prospects.
How quickly can we start on remediation?
Once you’ve completed your audit with Deque, you’re ready to start remediation. If you elect to have Deque conduct remediation on your behalf, it can start as soon as you provide Deque with access to your environment and source code–Deque can integrate with your existing workflow and codebase. And if you can’t provide access, Deque also offers a rapid remediation solution that does not involve updating the source code directly.
Our organization wants to be more inclusive and show our commitment to accessibility. What can we do?
Start by auditing your digital content and improving usability for all users. Publish an accessibility statement and outline your progress to demonstrate commitment and transparency. Check out
Deque’s Accessibility Statement
as an example.
How often should an organization perform accessibility audits?
Conduct accessibility audits annually or after major updates. Regular audits ensure ongoing compliance, prevent regressions, and maintain accessible experiences for all users.

The DHS Trusted Tester Process is a manual test approach that aligns with the ICT Testing Baseline, and provides repeatable and reliable conformance test results. There’s a plan for everyone
Just getting started? Turning side gigs into main gigs? Got more advanced needs such as monetizing multiple channels, working with clients or soundtracking tv shows and ads? Either way, we’ve got the perfect plan.
Soundtrack everywhere
Soundtracking with Epidemic Sound means you can publish content safely anywhere online, including the biggest platforms out there – as well as websites, games, apps, podcasts and more.
Better yet, the Pro plan covers up to three channels per platform, meaning less back and forth when editing channels and more time to focus on telling your story.
If you’re producing content for others, it’s easy to safelist content published on their channels. This means they won’t receive copyright claims that affect their right to monetize their content.
Need to soundtrack broadcast productions, in-person live events or exploring the metaverse? Get customized deal terms with our Enterprise plan.
some do’s
How am I allowed to use the music?
It depends on which plan you’re on. With the Creator plan, you can use our music in sponsored or branded content for your own channel(s), but you can't use our music in digital advertising, marketing, or promotion for a brand or company. You can with the Pro plan.
Explore our music
some don’ts
What isn't allowed?
Our music is intended to be used as background music for your video or podcast productions. You can use complete tracks and separate stems such as bass, instrumental, and vocals in your content, but you can’t use the music on a standalone basis, such as in audio samples, sound libraries, music beds, or via third parties.
Learn more about licensing
Frequently Asked Questions
Who can sign up for the Pro plan?
The Pro plan is for freelancers and businesses soundtracking commercial productions, excluding cinema, TV shows or TV ads. If you work for a publisher with a yearly revenue over USD 5 million or a company with a yearly revenue over USD 10 million, check out our
Business plans
. Business Plus covers a yearly revenue up to USD 25 million. For cinema, TV shows or TV ads, or a yearly revenue over USD 25 million, please
contact Enterprise sales
to get a customized license.
I’m a freelancer. Which plan is right for me?
The
Pro plan
gives you full sublicensing rights. If you produce content for others to publish on their channels and they want to avoid copyright claims, you simply add the URLs of the published video and we'll clear them for you.
Can I use the Pro plan for ad campaigns?
Yes, as long as it's an online campaign and you're not a government entity, a publisher with a yearly revenue over USD 5 million, or a company with a yearly revenue over USD 10 million. If you are, check out our
Business plans.
